In 2026Q2, Morgan Stanley stated it is investing in products like LeadIQ that will allow it to match individuals with advisers.

As of 2026-03-31, Morgan Stanley's CEO described co-piloting for financial advisers, with Jed Finn under Andy Saperstein spending time on corridors or super agents to drive efficiency and effectiveness across the wealth portfolio.
As of 2025-12-31, Morgan Stanley is leveraging technology to improve automation and facilitate client acquisition openings, as well as increasing education with its advisors and clients.

As of 2025-03-31, Morgan Stanley has ongoing investments in automation and AI, and in assessing where it wants its people over the next five to ten years, in the context of a reduction in XFA headcount.

On the 3Q26 earnings call, CEO Edward Pick described AI as a top priority for the firm's advisory role, saying the firm is now double overweight on AI and that it is existentially important that Morgan Stanley be viewed as a trusted adviser in the middle of the ecosystem.

On the 3Q25 earnings call, CFO Sharon Yeshaya described early AI use cases including LeadIQ, DevGen AI (enhancing developer efficiency), and Parable (an interactive tool analyzing and summarizing data).
On the 3Q26 earnings call, CFO Sharon Yeshaya stated the firm's scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.

On the 4Q25 earnings call, CEO Ted Pick stated the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
